thesis: Strong scores can conceal memorization, leakage, wrong objectives, group failures and misplaced confidence.
role: Develop a practical diagnostic discipline for model reliability.

ideas.statement: Training and validation errors distinguish overfitting from underfitting; regularization, early stopping and realistic augmentation constrain memorization.
Leakage includes unavailable-at-prediction features, shared entities across splits and preprocessing fitted on test data.
Precision and recall reveal error types hidden by accuracy, and thresholds should reflect the actual costs of false positives and false negatives.
Group audits, proxy checks and exploration address biased feedback, while calibration and out-of-distribution checks distinguish confidence from reliability.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Clever Hans reads involuntary cues; an always-negative fraud detector achieves high accuracy while detecting nothing.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Calibration depends on matching distributions, guarantees concern sets of cases, and no confidence statement proves one answer true.

audit.notes: Entire assigned segment reviewed; scope and qualifications preserved. Duplicate contents and publication metadata are not ranked as ideas.
